overview: Caddo peoples formed distinct river-valley communities connected by language and kinship. Their descendants continue as the Caddo Nation.

items.text: Independent named groups included villages, hamlets and farmsteads. Settlement patterns varied across the Caddo homeland.
Late seventeenth-century accounts describe community chiefs, or caddi, consulting elders called canahas. These accounts chiefly concern Hasinai communities.
Maternal descent and clans connected people across households; communal work included housebuilding, planting and harvesting.
Potters made cooking and serving vessels, pipes and ornaments. Jeri Redcorn helped revive an ancestral pottery tradition.
Archaeologists place an emerging Caddo phase around 800-1000 CE, when ritual centers developed among villages. This approximate cultural phase is not a founding year.
Dispossession forced survivors toward Indian Territory. Caddo people maintained and renewed their traditions through these transformations.
